b: Who knows if they'd peeped in while we were changing clothes, but at immigration they asked questions till our throats went dry. I'd slip through and get ahead. It was Dhanush they held back and talked to a lot.. Since it was two boys going to Vietnam alone, apparently they teased him like we were rainbow boys. Rami often worries that Dhanush has this kind of market.. Looks like it's true

Getting past their trouble, we somehow got on the plane.. Everyone was sitting there in comfort, and we started to cook.. And a real thirst too.. To cut costs we hadn't included food in the ticket. It was three hours to get to Malaysia .. Couldn't be patient till then, so I pressed the button, called the attendants and asked for a glass of water, and they held out the menu card.. My chest hurt a little.. Cursing them in my heart that people who won't give water to a thirsty mouth should become frogs, I thought I'd buy the water, and apparently you have to buy it in Malaysian money.. As if our dad had brought us loads back from Malaysia..Go away, you and your water, I said, and slept soundly, thirsty

The moment we landed in Malaysia, our first run was to the water fountain.. Bless them, they had lots of them.. We drank till our thirst was gone and looked around.. People were lying on the floor next to the charging points.. In hospitals we'd call them floor patients.. slightly less urgent patients you can't give a bed to.. If you go early in the morning, they'll be lying on mats on the floor.. In campus days, these were in great demand for clerking.. There wouldn't be many problems.. They'd be sent home the next day… but by chance there are some who stay a long time too.. That takes some luck as well

Thinking they wouldn't weigh us after this, I took the clothes off in the bathroom, sprayed some scent and stuffed them into the bag.. Since Dhanush had a lot to take off, he said he'd just go as he was.. We got through check-in for the next flight smoothly and went in

There, we found someone new to talk to. We both had window seats. On my other side sat a lady.. Once we're on board, you know our habits.. we were gabbing away without shutting our mouths..Suddenly she tapped us and asked in English, are you from Sri Lanka..We were amazed..Usually, when we speak Tamil, people ask if we're from India.. For the first time someone had guessed right

After that too she only spoke in English.. I'm writing that conversation in Tamil..Her roots are in Jaffna.. Her grandmother was born and raised there.. But they're the third generation .. Though their names are Tamil, they can't speak or write Tamil.. They're Malaysian Tamils now.. Still, she had the skill to work out which Tamil we were speaking..

She praised Sri Lankan Tamils as humble.. Though I felt proud, I also had a doubt whether that ring would fit everyone...She said she and her girlfriends were going to Vietnam to relax.. In that short time we talked a lot.
Looking down from the plane, it was as if the clouds were carrying us along.. Such a beautiful sight..As we sat enjoying nature like this, the flight landed
Just when we thought we'd switch on roaming data and tell everyone we'd arrived, another incident
